book: When Easy Is the Wrong Signal
excerpts: Most learners are convinced that smooth study is good revision. A page that reads easily feels learned, and a reader who meets no trouble closes the book satisfied. Open it a week before the exam, every line looks familiar, and we conclude too quickly that the material is safe. However, learners are unexpectedly poor judges of their own recall. What the eye can recognize, the hand often cannot recite. The gap appears

the moment the book is shut. The confident reader goes blank at the exam desk. A classmate who studied uneasily and answered uncertainly now writes the page out. The flaw in easy revision is that it can prove only how well we know the look of a sentence, not how well we can rebuild one. Work that feels worse does better: close the book, write the answer from recall, then check periodically what came out incorrectly.
